claim_verdicts.evidence: SDK 3.47.2 framework.dart:2201 BuildContext: 'A handle to the location of a widget in the widget tree.' ... 'BuildContext objects are passed to WidgetBuilder functions (such as StatelessWidget.build), and are available from the State.context member.' ... 'Each widget has its own BuildContext'. State.context: 'The location in the tree where this widget builds.'

navigator.dart Navigator.of: 'The state from the closest instance of this class that encloses the given context.' widgets/app.dart: 'The [Navigator] is only built if routes are provided (either via [home], [routes], [onGenerateRoute], or [onUnknownRoute])'. Reworded claim and lesson ('Here MaterialApp is given a home, so it creates one') now carry the condition; main.dart@stage-1 passes home: ProductListScreen(...).

navigator.dart Navigator.of doc: 'If there is no [Navigator] in the given `context`, this function will throw a [FlutterError] in debug mode, and an exception in release mode.' Assert text: 'Navigator operation requested with a context that does not include a Navigator.' theme.dart Theme.of doc confirms a build method's own context is 'above' the MaterialApp it returns: 'the `context` argument to the `build` function can't be used to find the [Theme] (since it's "above" the widget being returned)'.

material/theme.dart Theme.of: 'The data from the closest [Theme] instance that encloses the given build context.' theme_data.dart: ThemeData holds 'final ColorScheme colorScheme;' and 'final TextTheme textTheme;' (colours, text styles/fonts). Lesson: 'such as the app's colours and fonts' — supported; main.dart@stage-1 sets theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: ...).

git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.App/lib/screens/product_list_screen.dart lines 34-41: 'actions: [ IconButton( icon: const Icon(Icons.login), onPressed: () => Navigator.of(context).push( MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => LoginScreen(apiClient: widget.apiClient)), ), ), ],' — identical to the lesson block. context is the parameter of _ProductListScreenState.build (line 30).

git show stage-1:DonHang.App/lib/screens/login_screen.dart lines 29-33: 'await widget.apiClient.login(...); if (!mounted) return; Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement( MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => CreateOrderScreen(apiClient: widget.apiClient)), );' — identical to the lesson block; inside _LoginScreenState._submit, so context is State.context.

framework.dart State.mounted: 'Whether this [State] object is currently in a tree.' BuildContext.mounted: 'Accessing the properties of the [BuildContext] or calling any methods on it is only valid while mounted is true. If mounted is false, assertions will trigger. Once unmounted, a given [BuildContext] will never become mounted again.' State.context asserts: 'This widget has been unmounted, so the State no longer has a context (and should be considered defunct).'

product_list_screen.dart:11 @stage-1: 'const ProductListScreen({super.key, required this.apiClient});' — only apiClient is required, key optional; matches reworded claim and lesson 'requires only an ApiClient'. api_client.dart: 'One place that knows the api's base URL...' (the class that talks to the server). main.dart:16-22: DonHangApp.build returns MaterialApp, so its context is above it.

Not opinion as used in the lesson ('without the navigator being passed down through each constructor'): the stage-1 source shows ProductListScreen has no navigator parameter (product_list_screen.dart:9-11) yet line 37 obtains one with Navigator.of(context), which per navigator.dart returns 'the closest instance of this class that encloses the given context'.

navigator.dart Route doc: 'Most routes have visual affordances, which they place in the navigators [Overlay] using one or more [OverlayEntry] objects.' Navigator doc: 'display their logical history using an [Overlay] with the most recently visited pages visually on top of the older pages.' NavigatorState.build returns '... child: Overlay(key: _overlayKey, ... initialEntries: _allRouteOverlayEntries ...)', so route widgets are descendants of the Navigator.

framework.dart State.context: 'The location in the tree where this widget builds. The framework associates [State] objects with a [BuildContext] after creating them ... and before calling [initState].' State.mounted: 'Whether this [State] object is currently in a tree.' Both are State members, usable from any method (login_screen.dart:30-31 uses them in _submit). Validity after dispose is the mounted condition the lesson states next.

issues.text: Section 4 says every `build` method receives a context. But the sign-in code uses `context` and `mounted` outside any `build` method, and I was never told where they come from. `mounted` is only explained in prose, not in Core concepts, and Connections says it comes from a `State` class that a later lesson teaches. I cannot tell why `context` exists in the sign-in code.
issues.quote: So after the `await`, the code first checks `mounted`, which is true only while the screen is still in the tree.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before this one: in a screen's class like `_LoginScreenState`, `context` and `mounted` can be used in any method, not only in `build`, and the next lesson shows where they come from.

issues.text: The lesson says `push` puts `LoginScreen` 'on top of the stack', which I read as 'above everything'. Then Try it (item 3) and quiz q3 (b) say `LoginScreen`'s context finds the navigator, so it must sit below the navigator in the tree. Nothing in the lesson says that. The diagram does not show `LoginScreen`, so I would get item 3 and q3 wrong or just guess.
issues.quote: and `push` puts a new `LoginScreen` on top of the stack.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this: a screen pushed onto the navigator sits below the navigator in the widget tree (the 'top' of the stack is not above the navigator), so its context can find the navigator too.

issues.text: The dashed lookup arrow starts at `IconButton`, but section 5 says the context used belongs to `ProductListScreen`. I can't tell whose position the lookup starts from. Also, the section 4 prose never names the `IconButton` or `DonHangApp` nodes.
issues.fix: Start the dashed arrow at ProductListScreen, or add a sentence in section 5 saying the icon's `onPressed` uses the screen's `context`. In section 4, name `DonHangApp` as the example of 'a widget above it'.
